alerts.title: Progressive creatinine rise on TDF with regular ibuprofen use
alerts.message: Guidelines advise checking creatinine/eGFR regularly on TDF and, in patients on TDF, checking creatinine even when intercurrent illness is suspected because dehydration or sepsis can worsen renal function. Creatinine has risen steadily from 0.9 (2020) to 1.4 mg/dL (2026) with eGFR now 52 mL/min/1.73m2, and urinalysis shows protein 1+ and trace glucose, suggesting tubular involvement. Possible contributors are TDF nephrotoxicity and regular NSAID (ibuprofen 2-3 times weekly for 6 months) use, which can compound renal injury. Non-drug causes such as hypertension (BP is currently normal) or diabetes (none diagnosed) are not evident. The fatigue reported may warrant evaluation alongside renal function.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat creatinine, eGFR, urinalysis and urine protein quantification; counsel to stop or avoid ibuprofen; review TDF suitability with renal monitoring and consider switching to a less nephrotoxic NRTI backbone per guideline.

alerts.title: Viral suppression on DTG: continue routine 6-monthly monitoring
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend viral load every 6 months on DTG-based first-line ART, with continuation of the regimen if viral load is below 50 copies/mL. Viral load is <50 copies/mL with CD4 584 cells/uL and reported adherence above 95%, so virological control is satisfactory.

evidence.recommended_action: Continue TLD; next viral load in 6 months. Reduce to 12-monthly only if suppressed over 1 year with reliable adherence per guideline.
